title: run.v1
description: The record of one run of a pack. Lives in .agency/runs/<run-id>/run.json and is committed.

id.description: ULID of the run; also the name of its directory.

pack.description: Name of the pack this run used — a skill in .claude/skills/agency-<name>/.

slug.description: owner/repo, or null — a repository with no remote is a legitimate project; packs with no sinks do not need one.

target.description: What was reviewed. The key (repo, pr, headRefOid) guarantees idempotence — the same commit twice does not produce a duplicate.

kind.description: merged-pull-request is a retrospective audit — without it a pack has nothing to do on a project with a single merged PR. workspace is a run with no pull request: the project as it is right now, uncommitted work included — this is what QA, which tries the running application, stands on.

filesSkipped.description: Lockfiles, generated files, snapshots — noise for both the graph and the dimensions.

ref.description: The target branch of a workspace run. Left empty for a PR run.

dirty.description: Was there an uncommitted change in the working copy at start? A finding from such a run may point at code that exists nowhere else.

trigger.description: The trigger kind determines the credential kind. Attended → subscription, unattended → an API key with a budget. This has to be in the data, not in a promise.

heartbeatAgeSeconds.description: Age of the live session's heartbeat at start. When it is too old, the run is queued and does not proceed.

outputs.description: What the run left behind besides findings.json. The core does not produce these, only records that the pack wrote them.

summary.description: RUN_DIR/summary.md — a short summary in the specialist's own words: what it looked at, what it found, what it decided, what it recommends next.

handoff.description: RUN_DIR/handoff.md — a message addressed to the next member of the chain: what I did not finish, what not to trust, what rests on an assumption for them to confirm. Unlike summary.md, which is "what I did" for a human and for memory, this is "what you need". Falls back to summary.md when missing.

graph.description: State of the code-graph index during the run, including which driver served it. Without this you cannot tell in hindsight whether a finding stood on a fresh index or one a month old.

driver.description: Which code-graph driver served the run. Without this, after a driver swap you cannot tell whether findings dropped because of a worse tool or a missing capability.

capabilities.description: Which questions the driver answered during this run. A dimension that stands on a missing capability skips itself — and this is where you see why.

note.description: A limitation the pack ran into with the graph tool that the fields above cannot express — e.g. a query returning empty for a symbol confirmed present by direct reading. Free text, not machine-read; a place to keep a real observation from being silently dropped.

changedFunctionsTruncated.description: The graph truncated the list of changed functions (CRG: CRG_MAX_CHANGED_FUNCS, default 500). changedFunctions is then a lower bound, not a count.

cost.description: Without this there is no way to answer whether the system is worth it even at full API price — and that is one of the kill criteria. Has to exist before history accumulates that it cannot be filled in retroactively.

credential.description: Which credential paid for the run. Derived from the runner's environment (an API key in it means api-key, otherwise the subscription that the interactive login left behind), never from trigger.attended: `claude -p` is unattended and still runs on the subscription, so deriving it from attendedness produced a number that was simply wrong.

usd.description: What the runner itself reported the run cost. An estimate on a subscription rather than an invoice — recorded because the relative cost of two models over the same target is the comparison this tool exists to make, and refused as a budget ceiling for the same reason.

status.description: abandoned is not failed: preparation succeeded and the agent was launched, then the terminal was closed before it finished. Nothing here can see that terminal, so the run stays open until a person closes it - which makes an abandoned run a fact worth recording rather than an error to hide.

gated.description: dropped by the deterministic gate (no evidence, or no file:line)

agent.description: What handled the run. The model is part of the record because precision is compared between models, not only between packs.

hire.description: Historical: the roster id (e.g. review-graph@codex) a pre-v1 run was hired under, from the since-removed .agency/hires.json. New runs leave this null and are identified by pack + provider alone — there is no roster to name a second worker over the same pack.

exitCode.description: How the agent process ended. Only a run started with `agency run --wait` has one: `--launch` replaces this process and leaves nobody to catch it, and a command copied into another terminal is not watched at all. Non-zero means the run failed even if findings.json was written — status says failed and the findings stay.

authorized.description: What the agent was allowed to do. `grant` is the default — write into the working directory and the handed-over memory directory, plus the commands the pack's method declares in run.needs. `bypass` is a project opt-in that turns the checks off entirely. `ask` grants nothing: an attended agent asks, an unattended one is refused and finds nothing it can record. Written because "the run found nothing" and "the run was not allowed to write anything" are indistinguishable afterwards without it.

sessionId.description: The runner's own id for the session, when it reports one. Lets a run be replayed in the provider's tooling — `claude --resume <id>` — which is the only way to see what the agent actually did after the terminal is gone.

turns.description: How many turns the agent took. Only a streamed unattended run has one; attended runs inherit the terminal and nothing counts for them.

denied.description: Tool calls the permission model refused. A non-zero count means the run is not a measurement of the method — it is a measurement of its authorization, and comparing it against another run would be comparing different things.

tools.description: Distinct tool names that were refused, e.g. Write, Bash.

evidence.description: Deterministic signal gathered before the run, for a pack that does not run over the graph — how many files changed, how many commits landed, how many findings the project already knows.

gatedBy.description: How many findings the gate dropped and why — schema, phantom-file, phantom-line, below-score. Written by ingest; without a breakdown by reason you cannot tell what a pack most often wastes on.

worktree.description: POSIX path of the throwaway worktree the run holds while it is running. It is recorded so a parallel run by another specialist can tell an occupied directory from an abandoned one instead of force-deleting a review in progress.

chain.description: This run's membership in a chain of specialists (`agency chain`). Absent for a standalone run. Without this block you could not tell, from the runs alone, which decision was made over someone else's finding as a handoff and which was made independently — and that is the whole difference between a team and a few runs back to back.

id.description: ULID of the chain. Shared by all its runs.

position.description: The member's order in the chain, starting at one.

of.description: How many members the chain has. Recorded so a broken-off chain can be told apart from a finished one without reading the other runs.

upstream.description: Ids of the runs whose output this member received as input — in the order they ran. Empty for the first member.
